newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says Boeing merger offer "not enough".
newsitem.headline: Bonn says Boeing merger offer "not enough".

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday that concessions offered by Boeing Co to Europe over its merger with McDonnell-Douglas did not go far enough to satisfy German concerns.

"Boeing has offered things which are not enough," Rexrodt told a news conference. "The decisive things are the terms of exclusive contracts and the spill-over of military technology (into civilian areas) -- that is clearly not enough."
Boeing has failed to satisfy the European Union Commission that its merger would not create a market-dominating position against Europe's Airbus commercial aircraft consortium.
Rexrodt dismissed as insufficient Boeing's offer to cut new exclusive aircraft supply deals to 10 years, and to scale back existing exclusive contracts to 15 from 25 years.
German officials also said the Boeing merger would create potential for anti-competitive cross-subsidies from McDonnell Douglas' military business.
Germany's government aerospace coordinator Norbert Lammert also said that Bonn stood fully behind the Brussels commission in its negotiations with Boeing.
